Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES – March 3, 2022

A meeting of the Inglewood Park and Recreation Commission was convened on March 3, 2022, via
Zoom. Commissioner Denmon called the meeting to order at 6:00 p.m. followed by the flag salute.

Roll Call
Present
  Commissioner Lee Denmon, District One
  Commissioner Jacob Fragoso, District Two
  Commissioner Cynthia, McLemore, District Three
  Commissioner Christopher Beck, District Four
  Sabrina Barnes, Director-Parks, Recreation, and Community Services
  Geoffrey Okamoto, Transportation Supervisor
  Juan Mata, Parks Maintenance Supervisor
  Teresa Estrada, Recreation Superintendent
  Stephanie Maldonado, Senior Management Assistant
Absent
  Commissioner Henry Brown, Commissioner at Large

Public Comments

  None

Approval of the Minutes

  Commissioner Fragoso made the motion to approve the minutes from May 6, 2021.
Commissioner McLemore seconded and the minutes were approved as follows:
  Ayes: Commissioners McLemore, Fragoso, and Denmon
  Nays: None

  Commissioner Mc Lemore made the motion to approve the minutes from August 5, 2021.
Commissioner Denmon seconded and the minutes were approved as follows:
  Ayes: Commissioners McLemore, Fragoso, and Denmon
  Nays: None

  Commissioner Fargoso made the motion to approve the minutes from February 3, 2022.
Commissioner Mc Lemore seconded and the minutes were approved as follows:
  Ayes: Commissioners McLemore, Fragoso, and Denmon
  Nays: None

  1
   Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES – March 3, 2022

Staff Report

  Staff presented a staff report recommending the Park and Recreation Commission
recommend the Mayor and Council Members take the following actions:
  a) Approve Amendment Nine (9) of the Elderly Nutrition Program Services Subaward Number
  ENP202107 (City Agreement No. 20-201) with the County of Los Angeles Workforce
  Development Aging and Community Services (WDACS) to allocate CDA ARP Act funding
  in the amount of $236,000 for provision of the Elderly Nutrition Program (ENP) (Grants
  Fund); and
  b) Adopt a resolution amending the Fiscal Year 2021-2022 Budget to receive $236,000 from
  the County of Los Angeles Workforce Development Aging and Community Services for the
  provision of the Elderly Nutrition Program.

  Commissioner McLemore made the motion to approve the staff report and Commissioner
Fragoso seconded. The staff report was approved as follows:

  Ayes: Commissioners McLemore, Fragoso, and Denmon
  Nays: None

Public Comments

  None

Verbal Reports

  Geoffrey Okamoto gave a verbal report on behalf of the Human Services Division regarding
the following:
   Transportation: Our Senior and disabled transportation program continues to provide trips
  to critical appointments such as dialysis and doctors' appointments. Drivers, as well as
  passengers, continue to wear mandated face masks coverings. We have also been
  scheduling our drivers to transport our seniors and persons with disabilities to other next-
  day requested appointments. Super Bowl LVI provided our drivers and opportunity to assist
  in transporting several hundred safety personnel mainly police officers. Due to recent
  decline with the Omicron virus, we were able to re-introduce our local Inglewood Trolley
  which started back into service as of March 1, 2022. We hope to get back to normal
  transportation operations soon but also understand the concerns that our seniors may have
  in getting re-acclimated to a new normal.
   Nutrition: Our Nutrition program provides seven (7) meals per week to approximately 300
  senior residents of Inglewood. We continue to provide monthly shelf-stable meal packages
  in collaboration with the Los Angeles Food Bank, and weekly fresh produce deliveries in
  collaboration with the Social Justice Learning Institute.

  2
   Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES – March 3, 2022

    Summer Food Program: The Child and Adult Care Food Program (CACFP) provides 450
  Grab-N-Go meals per week to youth 18 and younger at three sites (Crenshaw Library,
  Rogers Park, and Darby Park).
    Senior Center Operations: The Inglewood Senior Center recently shutdown the limited
  classes and activities due to the recent Omicron variant surge as we continue to monitor its
  effects. We want to ensure our seniors are as safe as possible during this time. We recently
  re-opened our doors on March 1, 2022, to continue with the limited classes that had begun
  before the Omicron virus took effect. We hope to get back to normal operations soon to be
  able to better serve our seniors.
    Super Bowl LVI provided an opportunity for our senior center to house the EOC
  headquarters for the JOC, JIC, Human Trafficking Division as well as the Communication
  Center. All emergency personnel was well received and the emergency response teams
  were all able to provide the necessary emergency services for Super Bowl LVI.

  Commissioner Denmon asked are constituents getting the Grab-N-Go food. Mr. Okamoto
responded yes. Director Barnes explained the difference between the nutrition program and the
Grab-N-Go meals which is the youth nutrition program located at the parks. The seniors are still
receiving their meals by home delivery.

  Juan Mata gave a verbal report on behalf of the Parks Administration regarding the following:
    Parks Maintenance Division assisted:
  1. NFL 360 event at Edward Vincent Jr, Park: planting seven (7) 24" Camphor trees,
  70 flats of begonias, and 20 flats of primroses
  2. Replanting 35 flats of primroses and 20 flats of begonias on Hillcrest Boulevard in
  front of the United States Post Office.
    The Graffiti Abatement staff also assisted with the NFL 360 event at Edward Vincent Jr, Park
  painting a mural alongside the pool area walls and repainting the Amphitheater walls.

  Teresa Estrada introduced Brian Sousa, new Recreation Supervisor (oversees the Westside
Recreation Facilities, Rogers, Siminski, and Ashwood Parks). Mr. Sousa introduced himself and
shared his previous job experience, education, and the California Parks & Recreation Society
(CPRS) District 9 where he serves on the board.

  Brian Sousa gave a verbal report on behalf of the Recreation Division regarding the
following:
   Youth Baseball: We are excited to announce that the Los Angeles Dodgers Foundation has
  approved our 2022 Dodgers Dreamteam Affiliate Partner application. The City of Inglewood
  will partner with the Los Angeles Dodgers Foundation for the 2022 Youth Baseball Season.

  The foundation has approved a grant to support the Dodgers Dreamteam program with the
  City of Inglewood Parks, Recreation, and Community Services Department in the amount of

  3
   Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES – March 3, 2022

  $40,260. The grant will offset staffing to include a Dodgers Dreamteam Coordinator, field
  maintenance, and umpire fees. The grant will support 480 players ages 5-18. In addition to
  the grant funds, the foundation will provide in-kind contributions to include; uniforms,
  equipment, recruitment and marketing materials, educational & health resources, coach
  mentors and training, player development clinics, incentives, and giveaways. This year
  marks our 6th consecutive year collaborating with the Los Angeles Dodgers Foundation to
  bring the Dodgers Dreamteam Program to Inglewood. Over six years, we have served over
  1,500 youth from the local community. Our Spring League will begin on March 21st for T-Ball
  (ages 5-6) and Coach Pitch Divisions (ages 7-8) at Darby and Edward Vincent
  Park. Registration for these divisions will close on March 11.The Summer League for the
  older divisions (ages 9-18) including the Minors, Majors Junior, Senior and Softball divisions,
  will begin in June. Registration will be conducted from April 18 – to May 6,
  2022. Registration is taken on a first-come, first-serve basis. The cost is $15 per player. To
  register visit www.Dodgers.com/Dodgersdreamteam.
    STEM Fest: The Parks, Recreation, and Community Services Department in partnership
  with Science of Sport will host the first annual Inglewood STEM Fest on Saturday, April 9
  from 9:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. at Edward Vincent Park. The free event is open to local youth in
  grades kindergarten through sixth. The event will expose students to science, technology,
  engineering, and math (STEM) through unique experiences that focus on several familiar
  sports. The event will also show participants real-world applications of STEM that focus on
  kinesthetic learning, scientific methods, and curriculum that align with California Math,
  Science, and Physical Education standards. This inaugural event is designed to bring in Los
  Angeles-based sports organizations to provide an engaging day of STEM and sports to the
  Inglewood community. Activity stations will be set up throughout the event providing STEM
  lessons centered on basketball, soccer, volleyball, baseball, softball, football, and Olympics
  sports. The event will also feature a STEM presentation by Science of Sport and a panel
  discussion with industry professionals. The department is eager to collaborate on this joint
  effort. Our goal is to excite local youth about STEM and open students’ eyes to the possibility
  of a career in a STEM profession. Registration for the event is FREE and will open on March
  10. Register at www.parksrec.cityofinglewood.org.
  Commissioner Beck welcomed Brian Sousa.

Director’s Report

  Sabrina Barnes gave a verbal update regarding the following Capital Improvement Projects
currently in progress:
   Construction is underway for the pump track at Edward Vincent, Jr Park. Construction began
  on February 18, 2022. A groundbreaking will take place Wednesday, March 9, 2021 at 11:00
  a.m. This is phase one (1) of the project. There are plans to add other amenities and
  improvements. They will be leasing of an unused building as a bike hub where the public

  4
   Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES – March 3, 2022

  can come to get their bikes repaired, training on bike education, exposure to the pump track
  environment and awareness of cycling. We anticipate the track will be completed by early
  May.
    Also at Edward Vincent Jr, Park preparation is underway for repairing and replacing some
  of the playground surfacing pending Council for approval of the contract on either March 22,
  or April 5, 2022.
    Vincent Park restroom construction should be getting underway, notice has been given to
  proceed.
    Bids for the restroom project at Darby Park are due March 9, 2022, with an expectation to
  go before Council on April 9, 2022, for approval. Anticipating construction will start in May
  and be completed by December 22, 2022.
    Updating the RFP for the irrigation system at Vincent Park, no bids were received. Staff will
  re-issue the updated bid.
    Finalizing bid documents for the picnic area tables, covers, seats, and sinks at Edward
  Vincent Park. The arbors will look similar to those at Ashwood Park giving a more modern
  look.
    Darby Park basketball courts were renovated by Nike, Jumpman, and Shoe Palace.
    Sunday, March 6, 2022, HBO will unveil the outdoor courts at Roger Park renovation. HBO's
  new mini-series release: Winning Time" is based on the glory day of the Los Angeles Lakers
  a famous quote” If you didn't play ball at Rogers Park then you didn't play ball". A well-known
  artist that does art throughout Los Angeles County was contracted and created beautiful
  artwork on the courts and backboards.

  Commissioner Denmon asked if it was premature to put the artwork down so soon after the
rain. Sabrina Barnes stated the artwork has already been completed.

Public Comments

  Imhotep Coleman thanked the Commission and announced that on Sunday, March 6, 2022,
he will be taking some film scholars from his academy to shoot a short film at Darby. Commissioner
Beck asked Mr. Coleman what time is his event. Mr. Coleman stated from 8 a.m. until 5 p.m. between
the court and the open area adjacent to the baseball field.

Commissioner’s Comments

  None

With no further business, the meeting was adjourned at 6:32 p.m.
